body: `.gitignore` lines 14-15 are `*/__init__.py` and `__init__.py`, and line 17 is `tools`. Consequences, verified with `git ls-files` in session 16: lbm/backends/__init__.py has been untracked since T101 (the Backend protocol is not in the repo), and the whole of tools/ is untracked although CLAUDE.md documents `python -m tools.issues` and calls DOCS/ISSUES.jsonl committed. lbm/__init__.py and validate/__init__.py are tracked only because they predate the rule; flow/__init__.py was force-added in session 16. A fresh clone cannot import lbm.backends and has no issue queue tooling. Fix is to drop the two __init__.py lines and the `tools` line from .gitignore and add the missing files - but it touches lbm/ and repo-wide config, so it wants its own task rather than being folded into a product task (DOCS/PLAN2.md Risks, last row).
title: [repo] .gitignore drops every __init__.py: lbm/backends and tools/ are untracked

body:
`myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m validate.autoconfig --backend warp` prints FAIL. Section 1 (accuracy: Plan.estimated_seconds vs a timed run) predicted 5.61 s against an actual 3.78 s, error 48.3% against the rung's 25% limit. Section 2 is unaffected: all 24 sweep cases pass, worst peak |u| 0.0695, worst Re error 0.0000% - the same digits sessions 17 and 18 printed on numpy.

Pre-existing, not a T107 regression. Rung B had only ever been run on numpy (4.2% error in session 17, 15.0% in session 18), and D-059 calibrated the estimator against the numpy column of the DOCS/STATE2.md performance table. On warp the case is 360x390 = 140k cells, which sits between the table's measured 40k (4155 steps/s) and 1M (757 steps/s) rows, and a GPU at that size is partly launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound - so a log-log interpolation of two bandwidth-bound points over-predicts the time. The predictor is pessimistic (predicted slower than actual), which is the safe direction for a user-facing estimate but still outside the rung's own bar.

Fix would be either a warp-specific calibration point near 100-200k cells in the performance table, or an explicit fixed-overhead term in estimated_seconds for GPU backends. Neither belongs in T107.
dropped_reason: measured while this session's own orphaned processes were still running; superseded by a clean-machine measurement
title: [autoconfig] Plan.estimated_seconds is 48% out on the warp backend, so Rung B fails its accuracy check there

body:
`myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m validate.autoconfig --backend warp` prints FAIL. Section 1 (accuracy: Plan.estimated_seconds vs a timed run): predicted 5.61 s, actual 3.19 s, error 75.7% against the rung's 25% limit. Measured on an idle machine, AMD Ryzen 7 5800H at 3201 of 3201 MHz on mains, RTX 3050 Laptop, driver 592.82 (D-035).

Section 2 is unaffected on either backend: 24/24 sweep cases pass, worst peak |u| 0.0695, worst Re error 0.0000% - the same digits sessions 17 and 18 printed. Rung B on numpy is PASS the same day: predicted 61.05 s, actual 56.46 s, error 8.1%.

Pre-existing, not a T107 regression. Rung B had only ever been run on numpy (4.2% session 17, 15.0% session 18) and D-059 calibrated the estimator against the numpy column of the DOCS/STATE2.md performance table. The case is 360x390 = 140k cells, which sits between that table's measured 40k (4155 steps/s) and 1M (757 steps/s) warp rows; a GPU at that size is partly kernel-launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, so a log-log interpolation between two bandwidth-bound points over-predicts. The error is in the safe direction for a user-facing estimate (it promises more time than it takes) but is well outside the rung's own bar.

Matters for T110: M8's gate is a wall clock on warp, so an estimator 1.8x out on that backend is the one T110 will lean on. Fix is a warp calibration point near 100-200k cells in the performance table, or an explicit launch-overhead term in estimated_seconds for GPU backends. Neither belongs in T107.
title: [autoconfig] Plan.estimated_seconds over-predicts warp by 1.8x, so Rung B fails its accuracy check on the GPU backend
